predecessors.name: Duchy of Athens
predecessors.text: 'All of Attica and Boeotia passed peacefully into the hands of the Catalans' after Halmyros (15 March 1311)

successors.name: Acciaioli Duchy of Athens
successors.text: Athens, captured by Nerio I Acciaioli in 1388, and Neopatras, captured by him in 1390

ledger.x: 1311: the Catalan Company wins at Halmyros and takes the Duchy of Athens.
1312: the Company recognises the suzerainty of the Aragonese crown of Sicily.
1319: Alfonso Fadrique's Catalans begin the conquest of the Thessalian south.
1325: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa are Catalan.
1325: the Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly is complete ('by 1325'); the five-captaincy Duchy of Neopatras stands.
1348: the Serbs conquer Thessaly and the Catalans lose their Thessalian possessions.
1377: Peter IV of Aragon takes the ducal title.
1379: with Thebes lost to the Navarrese Company the seat is drawn at Athens.
1388: with Athens lost the only capital left is Neopatras ('the two capitals of Athens and Neopatras', Neopatras page; Athens fell in 1388).

wars.name: Battle of Halmyros and the Catalan takeover of the Duchy of Athens
wars.outcome: Decisive Catalan victory on 15 March 1311; Walter V of Brienne and almost the whole knighthood fell; Attica, Boeotia, Livadeia and Athens passed to the Catalans, Argos and Nauplia stayed with the Brienne loyalists.

wars.name: Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly
wars.outcome: The Catalans under Alfonso Fadrique take Neopatras in 1319 and the places named above by 1325 and organise the Duchy of Neopatras in five captaincies.

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Stefan Dusan's Serbs conquer Thessaly; the Catalans lose most of their Thessalian possessions and keep Neopatras.

wars.name: Navarrese Company conquest of Thebes
wars.outcome: The Navarrese Company conquers Thebes and part of the Duchy of Neopatras; by 1380 the Catalans hold only Athens, Neopatras and the County of Salona.

wars.name: Acciaioli conquest of Athens and Neopatras
wars.outcome: Nerio I Acciaioli captures Athens in 1388 and Neopatras in 1390, ending Catalan rule in central Greece.

certainty.note: Late medieval Aegean frontiers: the pages name cities and castles, never boundaries; no treaty line is drawn for any year.
